# Jane Andrews

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c33 P6](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0006), [v3 c5 P7](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0007)</sub>
- **Role:** school teacher  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mrs. Inglis  <sub>[v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Jane is described as a plain and steady girl with pink cheeks. Her mother ensures she is neatly turned out, though she was almost lost to sight under her wedding array of white satin, diamonds, tulle, lace, and orange blossoms.

_Sources: [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c41 P9](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0009), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## Personality

Jane is sensible, practical, composed, and conscientious, remaining steady and unflappable under pressure. Unpoetical by nature, she views poetry merely as lines and verses and prefers practical reality to romantic notions. She is placid, amiable, and lady-like, possessing the rare quality of never saying anything that would hurt anyone's feelings.

_Sources: [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c4 P8](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0008), [v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## History

Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of the Harmon Andrews family. During her school days, she joined Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Ruby Gillis in forming a Story Club and taking part in Miss Stacy's recitations. After preparing for the Entrance examination, she attended Queen's Academy in the Second Class work and took top honors in the domestic science course. She began her career teaching in Newbridge, where her success placed her name on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, and she helped found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Later, after a period of teaching in Avonlea, she moved to the West to teach on the prairies. During a holiday break, she proposed to Anne Shirley on behalf of her shy brother Billy, though Anne declined. Upon returning from the West, she married Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, and took a wedding tour to Europe before settling into a happy life where her wealth did not spoil her sweet and sensible nature.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c6 P10](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0010), [v2 c28 P3](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0003), [v3 c8 P12](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0012), [v3 c8 P17](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0017), [v3 c11 P0](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0000), [v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003), [v3 c39 P18](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0018), [v3 c39 P27](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0027), [v3 c39 P35](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0035), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## Quotes

> I guess we’ll get on all right. The main thing will be to keep order and a teacher has to be a little cross to do that. If my pupils won’t do as I tell them I shall punish them.  <sub>[v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002)</sub>

> But suppose they don’t?  <sub>[v2 c4 P8](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0008)</sub>

> I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever.  <sub>[v2 c13 P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)</sub>

> I should rather call it a picture. A poem is lines and verses.  <sub>[v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065)</sub>

> Billy wants to marry you. He’s always been crazy about you—and now father has given him the upper farm in his own name and there’s nothing to prevent him from getting married. But he’s so shy he couldn’t ask you himself if you’d have him, so he got me to do it. I’d rather not have, but he gave me no peace till I said I would, if I got a good chance. What do you think about it, Anne?  <sub>[v3 c8 P12](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0012)</sub>
